we achieve state of the art object detection performance using grid map representations for environment perception in autonomous driving.

(1) deep neural networks can be trained to detect and classify objects in grid maps, (2) the grid map resolution and the number of grid cells used for training have an influence on the performance of the network, (3) a grid map representation is a suitable input for deep neural networks for the task of object detection and classification, and (4) our method achieves state of the art detection performance on KITTI.

a novel approach of object detection and classification for autonomous driving applications using deep learning and grid maps.
the development and evaluation of deep neural networks for object detection and classification using grid maps.
a novel and efficient approach for environment representation, object detection and semantic segmentation using deep convolutional networks.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we provide a novel approach for environment segmentation in top-view grid maps using deep convolutional networks.
we are the first to show that a grid map representation is well-suited for deep learning and that it can be used for object detection and classification in top-view.
we show the applicability of grid maps as input for semantic segmentation tasks.
The main takeaway from our work is that
grid maps are a suitable representation to efficiently encode and process 3D data for semantic object detection and classification.
grid maps can be used as a powerful input for deep convolutional networks.
